newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Attacks on Iraq jolt share prices, boost oil.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Attacks on Iraq jolt share prices, boost oil.

text.p: News of U.S. missile attacks on Iraq gave a further boost to oil prices on Tuesday and jolted nervous European stock markets.
"It's going to be a very twitchy market this morning," said one senior London share dealer. "All eyes are on Iraq."
The U.S. punishment for weekend incursions by Iraqi troops into Kurdish areas also gave a limited boost to gold and the dollar, safe havens for funds at times of crisis.
But traders said the strength of the market reaction would depend on how events unfolded and they were focusing on a scheduled statement by President Bill Clinton at 1200 GMT.

In early business on London's International Petroleum Exchange, October futures for benchmark Brent crude rose 40 cents to $22.39 a barrel to add to a gain of $1.21 on Monday after the United Nations delayed implementation of an Iraqi oil-for-food deal. Brent earlier hit a high of $23.50 in Asia.
In the next few weeks, traders had been expecting Iraq's first oil sales for six years since the Gulf War to hit markets that were already around $4 higher than last year.

Gold prices gained around 50 cents an ounce to $387.40 in early European trade but then stabilised. "If the conflict does not escalate, prices are not likely to gain much. But now we have to wait and see," one dealer at a major Swiss bank said.
"I don't see gold at $400 because of this," another dealer said, adding traders remembered losing a lot of money during the 1990 Gulf War when gold prices soared and then collapsed.
"We had been expecting intervention. We didn't expect it to be military intervention," said a currency trader who had been anticipating central bank action to boost the dollar this week.

"As is usual in times of increased international tension, a generally dollar positive tone has been set, particularly against the yen, as the Japanese economy's exposure to higher oil prices depresses any yen positive sentiment," said Chris Tinker, chief treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
Currency traders said a Wall Street Journal article hinting at an imminent U.S. rate rise gave added stimulus to the dollar.
The London stock market, Europe's biggest, opened weaker and soon extended its losses, more than wiping out Monday's gains despite some compensation from higher oil company share prices.
Lower bond prices added to the downward pressure and traders forecast that investors would be cautious ahead of Wall Street's reopening after the U.S. Labor Day holiday on Monday.
French shares also headed lower in line with weaker bonds and with added concern over French economic problems, social unrest and pessimism over company profits.
"The attack by the Americans on Iraq is hitting the market," said one French trader. "Practically the only stocks showing plus signs are the oil stocks."
In Frankfurt, German shares also weakened although traders said concern over coming economic news was a more significant influence than the missile attacks on Iraqi air defence targets.

U.S. NAPM purchasing managers figures for August, due at 1400 GMT, and news on Friday of the key U.S. August non-farm payrolls data are key events in the statistical diary which could give clues on when interest rates are likely to rise.
A Reuter survey expected the NAPM index to rise to 52.9 from 50.2 in July but it could be even stronger, analysts said.
Second-quarter economic growth figures for France and Germany are also on the week's menu of statistics and could put further pressure on the French franc, analysts said.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 109.29 yen and 1.4880 marks, compared with 109.14 and 1.4863 in late European business on Monday. It earlier hit highs around 109.45 and 1.4912.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 26.7 points at 3,857.7.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index was 10.10 adrift at 2,522.78.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 19.00 at 1,957.98.
Tokyo's 225-share Nikkei average closed up 91.04 points at 20,198.15 after earlier dropping as low as 19,920.02.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $387.20 an ounce in the morning, up from the previous London close of $386.90 and afternoon fixing of $386.55. Silver gained one cent to $5.20.
